source_text:
θεραπεῦσαι τὴν ἀσθένειαν τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην καὶ τοῦ εὐσχημονέστατα οἰκονομῆσαι τὸ
κατὰ τοὺς τόπους· διόπερ εἶπεν ὀφειλὴν ὀφείλεσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς καὶ τῷ ἀνδρὶ
ἀπὸ τῆς γυναικός. εἶτα ἵνα μὴ δυσωπήσῃ τοὺς ἐν γάμῳ ὡς δούλους ἀλλήλων
τυγχάνοντας μὴ χωρὶς συμφωνίας ἥκειν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄσκησιν τῆς καθαρότητος φησίν· Ἡ
γυνὴ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλ' ὁ ἀνήρ· ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῦ ἰδίου
σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλ' ἡ γυνή. ἐξουσίαν οὖν ἔχει ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῦ σώματος τῆς
γυναικός, καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχων ἐὰν θέλῃ μὴ χρήσθω τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ· ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐχρη ά μεθα
τῇ ἐξου ίᾳ ταύτῃ, φησὶν ὁ ἀπόστολος, οἶμαι τοῦτο διδάσκων τῷ λέγειν μὴ οὐκ
ἔχομεν ἐξου ίαν ἀδελφὴν γυναῖκα περιάγειν, ὡ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπό τολοι καὶ οἱ
ἀδελφοὶ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ Κηφᾶ ; ἐξουσίαν οὖν ἔχει ἡ γυνὴ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ ἀνδρὸς
καὶ οὐ δύναται μὴ χρήσασθαι τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ; Τὸ δὲ ὁμοίως δὶς κείμενον δίδωσι νοεῖν ὅτι
μὴ νομιζέτω ὁ ἀνὴρ ἐν τοῖς κατὰ τὸν γάμον πράγμασιν ὑπερέχειν τῆς γυναικός·
ὁμοιότης ἐστὶ καὶ ἰσότης τοῖς γεγαμηκόσι πρὸς ἀλλήλους. 34 vii 5 [Μὴ ἀποστερεῖτε
ἀλλήλους, εἰ μή τι ἂν ἐκ συμφώνου πρὸς καιρὸν ἵνα σχολάσητε τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ
πάλιν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἦτε.] [Ὠριγένους] Ὀφείλετε γὰρ ἀμφότεροι εἰδέναι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν
ἡ αὐτὴ εὐχὴ ἀπὸ καθαρότητος ἀνδρὸς καὶ γυναικὸς καὶ εὐχὴ ἀπὸ κοινωνίας. εἰ γὰρ
ἐπὶ τῶν εἰδώλων Ἕλληνες ἔστιν ὅτε ἁγνεύουσι, πόσῳ πλέον σὺ ὁ τῷ θεῷ τῶν ὅλων
εὐχόμενος; καλὸν οὖν ἐστι συγκαταβαίνειν μὲν διὰ τὴν ἀσθένειαν, ἀνέχειν δὲ διὰ
τὰς εὐχάς. καὶ Μωϋσῆς μὲν ἁγνίζει τὸν λαὸν καὶ λέγει τρεῖ ἡμέρα μὴ προ έλθητε
γυναικί, ἵνα δυνηθῶσιν ἐκ τοῦ προκεκαθαρευκέναι ἀκροαταὶ γενέσθαι τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ
ἐν ταῖς Βασιλείαις δὲ ἁγίου ἄρτου βούλεται παραστῆσαι τῷ ∆αυεὶδ φεύγοντι τὴν
τοῦ Σαοὺλ ἐπιβουλὴν Ἀβιάθαρ ἢ Ἀβιμέλεχ ὁ ἱερεύς, καὶ βουλόμενος ἁγίου ἄρτου
παραθεῖναι τί φησι πλὴν Εἰ καθαρὰ τὰ παιδάρια ἀπὸ γυναικό ; οὐχ οἷον δὲ ἀπὸ
ἀλλοτρίας γυναικὸς ἀλλ' ἀπὸ γαμετῆς. εἶτα ἵνα μὲν ἄρτου προθέ εω λάβῃ τις,
καθαρὸς εἶναι ὀφείλει ἀπὸ γυναικό · ἵνα δὲ τοὺς μείζονας τῆς προθέσεως λάβῃ
ἄρτους, ἐφ' ὧν ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ
pass_a_gloss: to heal human weakness and to manage the matters in those places most seemly; therefore he said a debt is owed from the husband and to the husband from the wife. Then lest he shame the married as slaves of each other who must not come to purity’s discipline without agreement, he says: the wife does not rule her own body but the husband; likewise the husband does not rule his own body but the wife. So the husband has power over the wife’s body, and having power, if he wills, let him not use the power; but we did not use this power, says the apostle, teaching this I think when he asks whether we lack power to lead about a sister-wife as the remaining apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas. Does the wife then have power over the husband’s body and cannot refrain from using the power? The twice-set ‘likewise’ lets us see that the husband must not think he surpasses the wife in marriage matters; there is likeness and equality for the married toward each other. Do not deprive each other except perhaps from agreement for a season so you may have leisure for prayer and be together again. You both ought to know prayer from a man’s and woman’s purity is not the same as prayer from fellowship. If Hellenes sometimes live chastely before idols, how much more you who pray to the God of the whole? Good then to condescend through weakness and to hold off through prayers. Moses also cleanses the people and says for three days do not approach a woman so that by prior cleansing they may become hearers of God. And in Kingdoms Abathar or Ahimelech the priest wants to set holy bread before David fleeing Saul’s plot, and wanting to set holy bread what does he say except: if the young men are clean from a woman?—not from a strange woman but from a wife. Then to receive Presence bread one ought to be clean from a woman; but to receive greater breads than the Presence, over which God’s and Christ’s and the holy spirit’s name has been called, how much more ought one to be cleaner so as truly to receive the breads unto salvation and not unto judgment? Many think depriving is said only of gold or silver or such; yet the apostle clearly named deprivation also of those in marriages practicing chastity out of season and without agreement. Once simply, the one not rendering what is owed deprives the one to whom he owes by not rendering the owed. Sometimes a person is shut so he cannot pay two dues at once; therefore it is written that he may pay the necessary due. What I mean is clear thus: it is not possible both to pay prayers to God as one ought and for the married man to pay the due to the wife; therefore if the debt toward God presses, one must deprive the other. Hear him: do not deprive each other except perhaps from agreement for a season so you may have leisure for prayer and be together again—as if prayer sent up is not clean even for those who have come together, even if lawfully. One must also hold off from a woman in the time of the monthly flow, and it is counted a great charge to come together with a woman in the flow. In Ezekiel’s list of brave deeds and of sins it is written that he will not approach a woman in separation. And one must be wholly clean also from one’s own wife in a time of prayer and fasting. And again, he says, be together, lest Satan tempt you through your incontinence. This I say by concession, not by command. Everywhere he loosens the word through weakness and again tightens it to turn hearers. I wish all humans to be as I also am. But each has his own gift from God, one thus and another thus. Marriage breathes of gift when measures are kept—those of agreement. And one can truly say of some that for this man marriage is a gift when there is no unsettlement, when all peace, all agreement. Yet to say marriage of a believer with a Gentile or of a Gentile with a believer is a gift from God—I would not say that. For God’s gift cannot reach Gentiles; if she believes, if she is saved, then she will begin to receive the gift.
pass_b_english: to heal human weakness and to arrange the matters in those places most becomingly; therefore he said a due is owed from the husband and to the husband from the wife. Then, lest he shame those in marriage as being slaves of one another who must not come to the exercise of purity without agreement, he says: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband; likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife. The husband therefore has authority over the wife’s body, and having authority, if he wishes, let him not use the authority; “but we did not use this right,” says the apostle, teaching this, I think, when he says: Do we not have a right to take along a sister as wife, as also the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas? (1 Corinthians 9:5). Does the wife then have authority over the husband’s body and is she unable not to use the authority? The word “likewise” set twice gives us to understand that the husband must not think that in the matters of marriage he excels the wife; there is likeness and equality for those married toward one another.

Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, that you may have leisure for prayer, and be together again (1 Corinthians 7:5). You both ought to know that prayer from a man’s and a woman’s purity is not the same as prayer from intercourse. For if Greeks sometimes practice chastity before idols, how much more you who pray to the God of all? It is good, then, to condescend because of weakness, and to hold back because of prayers. Moses also purifies the people and says for three days not to approach a woman, that by having purified beforehand they may become hearers of God (Exodus 19:15). And in the Kingdoms, when Abathar or Ahimelech the priest wishes to set holy bread before David fleeing Saul’s plot, what does he say except: If the young men are clean from a woman?—not from a strange woman but from a wife (1 Samuel 21:4–5). Then, that someone may receive the bread of the Presence, he ought to be clean from a woman; but that he may receive the greater breads than the Presence, over which the name of God and of Christ and of the Holy Spirit has been invoked, how much more ought someone to be cleaner, that he may truly receive the breads unto salvation and not unto judgment?

Many think “deprive” is said only of gold or silver or something of that sort; but the apostle clearly named deprivation also concerning those in marriages who practice chastity unseasonably and without agreement. Once for all, simply, the one who does not render what is owed deprives the one to whom he owes by not rendering the due. Sometimes a person is shut in so that he cannot render two dues at once; therefore it is written that he may render the necessary due. What I mean will be clear thus: it is not possible both to render prayers to God as one ought and for the married man to render the due to the wife; therefore if the debt toward God presses, one must deprive the other. Hear him saying: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, that you may have leisure for prayer and be together again—as if prayer sent up is not pure even for those who have come together, even if they have come together lawfully. One must also abstain from a woman in the time of her period, and it is counted a great charge to come together with a woman who is in her period. In Ezekiel’s catalog of brave deeds and of sins it is written that he will not approach a woman in her separation (Ezekiel 18:6). And one must be wholly pure also from one’s own wife in a time of prayer and fasting.

And again, he says, be together, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self-control. This I say by way of concession, not of command (1 Corinthians 7:5–6). Everywhere he loosens the word because of weakness, and again tightens it to turn the hearers. I wish all people to be as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that (1 Corinthians 7:7). Marriage breathes of gift when the measures are kept—those of agreement. And one can truly say of some that for this one marriage is a gift, when there is no disorder, when there is all peace, all agreement. Yet to say that marriage of a believer with a Gentile woman, or of a Gentile with a believing woman, is a gift from God—this I would not say. For the gift of God cannot reach the Gentiles; if she believes, if she is saved, then she will begin to receive the gift.

choices.why: Origen extends ‘deprive’ from money to marital due without agreement.
